sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor Unity
    participant DM as DeckManager (Singleton)
    participant OD as ObjectsData

    rect rgb(230,245,255)

      loop For each selected card ID

        UM-->>DM: count
        alt count == 0 or missing

        end
      end
    end

    alt Any removals

    end

_:warning: Potential issue_

*Incorrect coordinate transformation may cause VFX positioning issues.*

The code is computing local coordinates relative to `_parent`, but the VFX manager later treats these as world coordinates (line 77-78 in RewardVFXManager.cs). This mismatch could cause VFX to spawn at incorrect positions.

The coordinate system should be consistent. Either:

1. Store world coordinates and use them directly, or
2. Store local coordinates and apply proper transformation when spawning

Apply this diff to store world coordinates instead:

-            var t = rewardItem.transform;
-            Vector3 localToParent = _parent.transform.InverseTransformPoint(t.position);
-            Quaternion localRotToParent = Quaternion.Inverse(_parent.transform.rotation) * t.rotation;
-
             _vfxQueue.Add(new RewardVFXManager.RewardVFXRequest
             {
                 Type = reward.RewardType,
                 Amount = reward.Amount,
-                Anchor = t,
-                WorldPosition = localToParent,         // Now relative to _parent
-                WorldRotation = localRotToParent,
+                Anchor = rewardItem.transform,
+                WorldPosition = rewardItem.transform.position,
+                WorldRotation = rewardItem.transform.rotation,
                 HasWorldPose = true
             });

*Null-guard button wiring; avoid NRE if Button missing*

If closeButton or its Button component isn’t set, Start() will throw. Guard it (or serialize a Button directly).

attachments.text:
## Walkthrough

Shifted time-based features to a timestamp-driven, additive scheduling model. Introduced a new addToCurrentTime parameter in TimeManager.Schedule, updated win-streak freeze, infinite lives, and timed boosters to use execution-time checks and additive extensions, and adjusted active-state Determination to compare stored execution times against current time.

## Changes

| Cohort / File(s)                                                             | Summary of Changes                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                          |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| *Core scheduling API*Assets/Scripts/Player/TimeManager.cs                    | Added Schedule(..., addToCurrentTime) parameter. When an execution time exists: if past, reset to now+delay; if future and addToCurrentTime=true, increment by delay. Added logging. HasExecutionTime logs result. RemoveScheduledAction no longer deletes PlayerPrefs key. |
| *Win-streak freeze (timestamp-driven)*Assets/Match3D/Game/StatTracker.cs     | IsWinStreakFreezeActive reads stored execution time, treats future timestamp as active, schedules remaining time if needed, otherwise returns false; falls back to HasScheduledAction when no timestamp. Activation now calls Schedule with addToCurrentTime=true.          |
| *Infinite lives (execution-time based)*Assets/Scripts/Player/LivesManager.cs | IsInfiniteLivesActive now uses HasExecutionTime and compares execution time to now. Activation methods unconditionally call Schedule with addToCurrentTime=true, removing prior branching on active state. Startup handling for existing execution time retained.           |
| *Timed boosters via TimeManager*Assets/Store/PlayerData.cs                   | Replaced PlayerPrefs DateTime storage with TimeManager scheduling. Activation schedules with addToCurrentTime=true. Active checks and remaining time computations use stored execution time from TimeManager; removed binary parsing and save writes.                       |

  user->>Feature: Activate(duration)
  Feature->>TM: Schedule(key, duration, onComplete, addToCurrentTime=true)
  alt existing future execution time
    TM->>TM: executionTime += duration
  else no or past execution time
    TM->>TM: executionTime = now + duration
  end
  TM-->>Feature: scheduled
  end

  rect rgb(245, 235, 255)
  note over Feature,Clock: Active-state check (timestamp-driven)
  Feature->>TM: HasExecutionTime(key) / GetExecutionTime(key)
  alt executionTime exists and executionTime > now
    Feature-->>user: IsActive = true
  else executionTime missing or <= now
    Feature-->>user: IsActive = false
  end
  end

  rect rgb(235, 255, 240)
  note over TM,Feature: Expiry callback
  Clock-->>TM: time reached
  TM->>Feature: onComplete()
  end

## Summary by coderabbit

• New Features  
   • Centralized UI event queue orchestrates post-level VFX, Daily Login, Season Pass popups, and tutorials.  
   • Input is automatically blocked during reward animations and restored afterward.  
   • Tutorials can be paused/resumed via the queue; active status is exposed.
• Improvements  
   • Season Pass start popup now launches reliably from the queue.  
   • Daily Gift advances the queue when ineligible, unclaimable, or closed.  
   • VFX sequencing waits for all animations to finish before proceeding, ensuring smoother flows.

## Walkthrough

Introduces a centralized UI.MainMenu QueueManager to sequence events (VFX, daily login, season pass, tutorials). Refactors VFX playback to coroutine-driven with active tween tracking and timeout. Adjusts SeasonPass and Daily Gift flows to integrate with the queue. Adds tutorial gating helpers and status exposure.

## Changes

| Cohort / File(s)                                                                                                                      | Summary                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| *Queue orchestration (new)*Assets/Scripts/UI/MainMenu/QueueManager.cs, Assets/Scripts/UI/MainMenu/QueueManager.cs.meta                | Adds MonoBehaviour-driven static queue for UI events; enqueues startup events; processes sequentially with tutorial gating; exposes EnqueueEvent and ProcessNextEvent.                                             |
| *VFX sequencing and synchronization*Assets/RewardVFXManager.cs                                                                        | Replaces direct sequencing with coroutine-based flow; tracks active tweens; waits for completion or timeout before advancing queue; adds PlayInitialVFX() entry point; registers tweens from reward/liveops paths. |
| *Season Pass popup flow integration*Assets/Scripts/LiveOps/SeasonPass/SeasonPassController.cs                                         | Adds _allowStartPopupFromQueue; gates HandlePopups; wires popup close to resume queue; updates NotJoined flow; standardizes to QueueManager.ProcessNextEvent().                                                    |
| *Tutorial gating and status*Assets/Scripts/Tutorial System/TutorialManager.cs, Assets/Scripts/Tutorial System/TutorialEventManager.cs | Exposes tutorial activity state and queue; adds BlockTutorials()/UnblockTutorials(...); adds GetPreDailyGateTutorialAsset() with priority lookup.                                                                  |
| *Daily Gift queue integration*Assets/Scripts/UI/Daily Gift/DailyGiftController.cs, Assets/Scripts/UI/Daily Gift/DailyGiftListener.cs  | Calls QueueManager.ProcessNextEvent() on disable and when login constraints prevent showing; replaces Start with public LoadDailyLogin().                                                                          |

_:warning: Potential issue_

*RunTutorial wait condition will never complete*

You never set finished, and current predicate requires IsPlayingTutorial && !TutorialActive which won’t become true with current TutorialManager behavior. Wait hangs the queue.

Apply this change to use a completion callback or a simple state check:

@@
-            HL.Log(HC.WorldMap, $"[Queue] Playing tutorial: {asset.name}");
-            bool finished = false;
-
-            TutorialManager.Instance.Play(asset);
-
-            yield return new WaitUntil(() =>
-                finished || (TutorialManager.Instance.IsPlayingTutorial && !TutorialManager.Instance.TutorialActive));
+            HL.Log(HC.WorldMap, $"[Queue] Playing tutorial: {asset.name}");
+            bool finished = false;
+            TutorialManager.Instance.Play(asset, () => finished = true);
+            yield return new WaitUntil(() => finished || !TutorialManager.Instance.IsTutorialPlaying());

> Committable suggestion skipped: line range outside the PR's diff.

:robot_face: Prompt for AI Agents 

```
In Assets/Scripts/UI/MainMenu/QueueManager.cs around lines 84 to 91, the
WaitUntil predicate will never become true because the local variable finished
is never set and the predicate uses (TutorialManager.Instance.IsPlayingTutorial
&& !TutorialManager.Instance.TutorialActive) which contradicts current
TutorialManager behavior; fix by using a real completion signal: update the call
to TutorialManager.Instance.Play to accept a completion callback (or subscribe
to its finished event) and set finished = true in that callback, or
alternatively change the WaitUntil predicate to poll for the tutorial no longer
playing (e.g., !TutorialManager.Instance.IsPlayingTutorial or
!TutorialManager.Instance.TutorialActive depending on the manager's semantics)
so the coroutine can resume.

```

_:warning: Potential issue_

*Tutorial never finishes: _isPlayingTutorial is set incorrectly and _currentTutorial is never cleared*

At the end of PlayCoroutine you set _isPlayingTutorial = true (should be false) and never null out _currentTutorial. This will deadlock QueueManager’s RunTutorial wait.

Apply this fix:

@@
-        callBack?.Invoke();
-        
-
-        GameEventsManager.SafeSendEvent(new TutorialCompletedEvent());
-        _isPlayingTutorial = true;
+        callBack?.Invoke();
+        GameEventsManager.SafeSendEvent(new TutorialCompletedEvent());
+        _isPlayingTutorial = false;
+        _currentTutorial = null;

:memo: Committable suggestion 

> :bangbang: *IMPORTANT*  
> Carefully review the code before committing. Ensure that it accurately replaces the highlighted code, contains no missing lines, and has no issues with indentation. Thoroughly test & benchmark the code to ensure it meets the requirements.

 Suggested change

| callBack?.Invoke();                                            |
| -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| _isPlayingTutorial = false;                                    |
|                                                                |
| GameEventsManager.SafeSendEvent(new TutorialCompletedEvent()); |
| _isPlayingTutorial = true;                                     |
| }                                                              |
| callBack?.Invoke();                                            |
| GameEventsManager.SafeSendEvent(new TutorialCompletedEvent()); |
| _isPlayingTutorial = false;                                    |
| _currentTutorial = null;                                       |
| }                                                              |

:robot_face: Prompt for AI Agents 

```
In Assets/Scripts/Tutorial System/TutorialManager.cs around lines 86 to 91, the
coroutine exit logic incorrectly sets _isPlayingTutorial = true and never clears
_currentTutorial, causing QueueManager to deadlock; change the flag to
_isPlayingTutorial = false and set _currentTutorial = null before returning
(preserve the GameEventsManager.SafeSendEvent and callBack invocation order as
needed) so the system recognizes the tutorial has finished.

```

## Walkthrough

Adds new analytics tracking methods for FPS and dynamic quality changes; integrates force-kill detection into app lifecycle; introduces a PerformanceTracker MonoBehaviour that reports scene FPS after a warm-up; updates QualitySetter to log when quality is adjusted; includes the corresponding Unity .meta file.

## Changes

| *Quality adjustment analytics*Assets/Scripts/Utils/QualitySettings/QualitySetter.cs | On low FPS threshold breach, after adjusting quality, calls AnalyticsManager.Instance.TrackAdjustingQualityDynamically with active scene name and FPS.                                                      |

### Bug: Force Kill Detection Logic Flaw

The `CheckForForceKilledApp` logic is inverted. It incorrectly flags quick app restarts as force kills when `timeSinceLastActive` is small, because `OnApplicationPause` or `OnApplicationQuit` update the last active time during normal exits. A true force kill would prevent this update, resulting in a _larger_ `timeSinceLastActive`.

_:hammer_and_wrench: Refactor suggestion_ | _:large_orange_circle: Major_

*Gate by previous graceful exit flag to avoid false-positives.*

Use the persisted flag; only report if the previous session didn’t quit gracefully and the interval is <30s.

Apply this diff:

         private void CheckForForceKilledApp()
         {
             var lastActiveTime = DominoPlayerPrefs.GetLastActiveTime();
             var timeSinceLastActive = HarmonyTime.GetServerDateTime() - lastActiveTime;
+            var lastExitWasGraceful = PlayerPrefs.GetInt(LastExitWasGracefulKey, 1) == 1;
 
-            if (timeSinceLastActive.TotalSeconds < 30.0f && AnalyticsManager.Instance != null)
+            if (!lastExitWasGraceful && timeSinceLastActive.TotalSeconds < 30.0f && AnalyticsManager.Instance != null)
             {
                 AnalyticsManager.Instance.TrackUserForceKilledApp();
             }

_:warning: Potential issue_ | _:red_circle: Critical_

*Fix the level key to reference the level that actually finished.*

`PlayerPrefs.GetInt("Level")` already points to the _next_ level by the time `HasCompletedPreviousLevel()` turns true, so the new key ends up being `LevelCompleteVFX_Shown_{N+1}` after beating level N. When the player later clears level N+1, the VFX is skipped entirely because that key is already marked, so the reward animation (and any side effects you attach to it) never fires. Please derive the key from the level that just finished—e.g., use `LastLevelCompleted` (or the LevelManager API that exposes the completed level id)—before saving it.

Suggested fix sketch:

-            int currentLevel = PlayerPrefs.GetInt("Level", 0);
-            string vfxKey = $"LevelCompleteVFX_Shown_{currentLevel}";
+            int lastCompletedLevel = PlayerPrefs.GetInt("LastLevelCompleted", -1);
+            if (lastCompletedLevel < 0)
+            {
+                return;
+            }
+            string vfxKey = $"LevelCompleteVFX_Shown_{lastCompletedLevel}";

_:warning: Potential issue_ | _:red_circle: Critical_

*Snapshot `CollectAndWinLocal.Collected` before iterating*

The loop keeps re-reading `CollectAndWinLocal.Collected`. If another system updates that static while the coroutine is running (e.g., a fresh token arrives or a sync resets it to 0), we either consume tokens that should belong to the next run or end up dividing by zero and waiting forever. _:warning: Potential issue_ | _:red_circle: Critical_

*Guard against missing EndlessModeManager instance.*

In non-Endless scenes we don't spawn an `EndlessModeManager`, so dereferencing `EndlessModeManager.Instance` will null-ref during `Start()`, breaking the Collect & Win HUD in the very modes this fix targets (regular levels, boss arena, endless toggle off). Wrap the lookup so we treat a missing manager as “not initialized.”

-        counterPanel.SetActive(!isLocked && !EndlessModeManager.Instance.IsInitialized);
-        IconPanel.SetActive(!isLocked && !EndlessModeManager.Instance.IsInitialized);
+        var endlessModeManager = EndlessModeManager.Instance;
+        var isEndlessInitialized = endlessModeManager != null && endlessModeManager.IsInitialized;
+
+        counterPanel.SetActive(!isLocked && !isEndlessInitialized);
+        IconPanel.SetActive(!isLocked && !isEndlessInitialized);

| counterPanel.SetActive(!isLocked && !EndlessModeManager.Instance.IsInitialized);           |

_:warning: Potential issue_ | _:large_orange_circle: Major_

*Initialize shadow color when the toggle is enabled*

`ApplyShadowColor` only runs via `UpdateToggle`, so when the toggle starts enabled (or disabled) the shadow sticks with the default `ShadowColorPreset.Black` until the user interacts. That regresses the intended polish for first render. Call `ApplyShadowColor` from `OnEnable` (using the current toggle state) so the shadow color matches the initial mask state.

     public void OnEnable()
     {
         if (isOnByDefault)
         {
             if (toggle.isOn) 
             {
                 mask.enabled = false;
             }
         }
+

• *Bug Fixes*  
   • Prevents premature progression during reward animations by waiting for Collect & Win status when available.

<https://github.com/owen.baker|@owen.baker> No, that's a valid concern about performance. Checking every frame is inefficient. Here are better alternatives:

*Option 1: One-time delayed check (recommended)*  
Add a coroutine that checks once after a short delay, giving the managers time to initialize:

void Start()
{
    Instance = this;
    var lockLevel = LevelVariantManager.CollectAndWinUnlockLevel;
    isLocked = lockLevel < 0 || LevelManager.Instance.GetCurrentLevelNumber() < lockLevel;
    bottleIcon.sprite = Colors[CollectAndWinLocal.GetCurrentColorIndex()];
    currentCount = 0;
    
    StartCoroutine(InitializeVisibilityDelayed());
}

private bool isLocked;

private IEnumerator InitializeVisibilityDelayed()
{
    // Wait one frame to let other managers initialize
    yield return null;
    
    var endlessModeManager = EndlessModeManager.Instance;
    var isEndlessInitialized = endlessModeManager != null && endlessModeManager.IsInitialized;

    var infiniteBossManager = InfiniteBossManager.Instance;
    var isInfiniteBossInitialized = infiniteBossManager != null && infiniteBossManager.IsInitialized;

    bool shouldShow = !isLocked && !isEndlessInitialized && !isInfiniteBossInitialized;
    counterPanel.SetActive(shouldShow);
    IconPanel.SetActive(shouldShow);
}

*Option 2: Event subscription*  
If `EndlessModeManager` and `InfiniteBossManager` fire events when they initialize, subscribe to those and update visibility once when they fire.

*Option 3: Check in OnEnable instead*  
If these managers initialize before scenes load, moving the check to `OnEnable()` might be sufficient.

Do the managers expose any initialization events, or does waiting one frame consistently solve the timing issue in your testing?
